newsitem.title: USA: Presumed Heaven's Gate cultist commits suicide.
newsitem.headline: Presumed Heaven's Gate cultist commits suicide.

text.p: A man believed to be a member of the Heaven's Gate cult committed suicide on Tuesday, more than a month after 39 cult members died in a strange mass suicide ritual, police said.
A spokesman for the San Diego County Sheriff's Department said another man, also believed to be a cult member, tried to kill himself but he was still alive and being treated at a local hospital.
The bodies were discovered at a Holiday Inn in nearby Encinitas, California.
The identities of the two presumed cult members were not immediately known and neither was the suicide method.

The bodies of 39 Heaven's Gate members were found on March 26 in an exclusive home in the Rancho Santa Fe suburb of San Diego. The 21 women and 18 men, between the ages of 20 and 72, were dressed in similar outfits, almost as if they were wearing uniforms. Police said the victims believed they would join up with a UFO behind the Hale-Bopp comet.
They died by eating drug-laced pudding or applesauce washed down with vodka and then placing plastic bags over their heads.
CNN television reported on Tuesday that it had received a videotape from the two men in which one of them said he hoped they had not "missed the bus."
The "Heaven's Gate" cult helped design computer web pages.
At the time of their death, the cult members made videotapes in which they expressed their pleasure at going to "a higher level".
Tuesday's suicide was the second time someone had tried to imitate the mass suicide.

On April 1, a 58-year-old recluse was found dead in his home in a remote mountain canyon in northern California after committing suicide and leaving a note indicating he believed he would join the dead Heaven's Gate cult members.
